<reason>CON (A) built a tighter, more sustained case around two load-bearing objections that PRO never fully neutralized: (1) conditional contracts do not solve the endogeneity/causal-attribution problem (stimulus correlates with worsening conditions), which PRO's "narrower conditioning" answer only restates rather than resolves; and (2) the accountability PRO touts ("money moving a price cannot be ignored") actually depends on externally imposed governance rules (mandatory documentation of divergence) rather than being an intrinsic property of markets — a point CON pressed consistently and used devastatingly in the closing to flip PRO's own central metaphor. CON also exposed PRO's rhetorically appealing but substantively weak move (B2.7) that equated ordinary transparency/scoring reforms with "secretly being a prediction market," correctly noting accountability doesn't require tradable stakes. PRO's incentive-based case (no skin in the game, Google/Metaculus examples, "auditable vs. invisible capture") was intuitive and well-argued, and its comparative framing of the burden was fair, but PRO repeatedly conceded parity rather than superiority on causal identification and ultimately grounded its enforcement mechanism in the same governance rules CON said could be applied without subsidized markets. Both sides handled the pressure-question format correctly with clear A1/A2 answers, but CON's answers did more damage while PRO's answers half-conceded ground. CON's closing, benefiting from true final chronological position, directly dismantled PRO's signature line, giving CON the cleaner final framing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's closing rebuttal directly quoting and refuting PRO's central closing claim ("Rules can be ignored; money moving a price cannot be") by showing that price movement alone does not force any official action — only institutional documentation rules PRO conceded were governance features, not market features — was the most decisive exchange, since it collapsed PRO's core asymmetry argument at the last possible moment.</best_rebuttal>
